description: The bar chart illustrates the number of morphosyntactic probing tasks performed on multilingual BERT models, categorized by language family or group, as presented in the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models.” The vertical axis lists ten language categories: IE-Slavic, IE-Romance, IE-Germanic, Uralic, IE-Baltic, IE-other, IE-Indic, Semitic, Turkic, and Basque, arranged in descending order of task count. The horizontal axis, labeled “# tasks,” ranges from 0 to 80 in increments of 10, representing the total number of probing tasks per category. IE-Slavic leads with approximately 79 tasks, followed by IE-Romance at around 47, and IE-Germanic at about 44. Uralic has roughly 20 tasks, IE-Baltic about 17, and IE-other approximately 15. IE-Indic and Semitic each have around 10 tasks, while Turkic and Basque trail with approximately 5 and 3 tasks respectively. Each bar is uniquely colored, though no legend is provided, and the bars are sorted from highest to lowest, visually emphasizing the dominance of Indo-European subgroups—particularly Slavic—in the probing evaluation.
